items.title: How one week of war has changed Iran, and what it could mean for the future
items.description: While the country's strict Islamist regime has blocked the internet and other forms of communication for most people, some have found a way to get their stories out.

items.description: Follow live.

items.title: Iran's regime change unlikely but Trump's mess certain: Gulf states
items.description: While the cabaret of outlandish and contradictory statements and claims continues in Washington, there is considerable pragmatic pessimism in the Gulf about the mess Donald Trump will leave behind.

items.title: All at sea with Pete Hegseth: Is this what AUKUS looks like in practice?
items.description: It seems that Australia finds itself yoked to America's actions whether the government likes it or not.

items.title: Trump's missiles don't just rattle oil markets; you'll feel it in your bills
items.description: Australia is a gas "superpower", but its citizens continue to pay the price through their electricity bills for the country failing to protect them from the fallout as the Middle East unravels again.

items.title: The 20-year search for the Nannup Four
items.description: In July 2007, Simon Kadwill, Tony Popic, Chantelle McDougall and her five-year-old daughter Leela vanished from an isolated WA town. Chantelle's parents have spent the better part of 20 years trying to work out how to live with what's happened, as a complex picture of deceit, coercive control and cult-like beliefs has come to light.

items.title: Social cohesion is fragile, but Australia can rebuild it, Anne Aly says
items.description: Radicalisation expert turned federal minister Anne Aly says reaching out to people susceptible to extremism and helping them reconnect to their communities is essential.

items.title: Community outrage as respected senior doctor escorted from hospital
items.description: Community outrage flares as a "respected and trusted" senior doctor is escorted from a regional hospital amid the fall-out from a controversial redevelopment project.

items.title: Trump demands 'unconditional surrender' from Iran, as US and Israel intensify strikes
items.description: The Israel military claims to be targeting "Hezbollah infrastructure" in the southern parts of the Lebanese capital — referred to as Dahiyeh.

items.title: 'Most brazen acts of corruption': Obeid family loses $30m worth of property
items.description: After investigations spanning a decade, the NSW Crime Commission says it has taken control of more than $30 million worth of properties linked to former New South Wales Labor politician Eddie Obeid.

items.title: 'Pray we don't get there': Analysts forecast huge surge in petrol prices
items.description: US crude oil has posted its biggest weekly gain in futures trading history, with the war in the Middle East leading to a major disruption to global fuel supplies.

items.title: Satellite imagery shows strikes around Iranian school where girls were killed
items.description: ABC NEWS Verify has analysed footage and satellite imagery to investigate what happened at a girl's elementary school in Minab, Iran.

items.title: LNP smashes 'break glass in case of emergency' box of distractions
items.description: The government made a flurry of other policy announcements to distract from its 11th-hour changes to its hate speech laws, writes state political reporter Alex Brewster.

items.title: Katherine 'under threat' as 'major flood' risk to remain until Sunday
items.description: Residents in Katherine woke up to find their main street had been submerged by flooding despite advice from authorities yesterday that the centre of town wouldn't be inundated. The river is expected to peak at 19.2m tonight.

items.title: Cory Bernardi stands by bestiality claim ahead of SA election
items.description: One Nation's South Australian lead candidate Cory Bernardi says he "100 per cent" stands by highly controversial comments he made almost 14 years ago linking gay marriage to the social acceptance of bestiality.

items.title: Russia makes Paralympics return amid calls for peace at opening ceremony
items.description: The Russian flag is flown at the Winter Paralympics for the first time in more than a decade, with Ukraine among eight countries to boycott the opening ceremony at Verona Arena in protest.

items.title: Why more Queensland couples are opting out of traditional weddings
items.description: In 2025, about 13 per cent of all wedding ceremonies in Queensland were held at registries as a growing number of couples opt to spend less on their big day.

items.title: RBA questions 'specialness' of US dollar in The Big Apple
items.description: The US dollar's status as a safe-haven currency is questioned at a business gathering in New York.

items.title: These are Australia’s best medal chances at the Winter Paralympics
items.description: Australia is about to head into the 2026 Winter Paralympics with one of its biggest, and quite possibly strongest, teams ever.

items.title: The little-known team representing Australia in powerchair hockey
items.description: The Sliders are representing Australia on the world stage in just two months, but they're not as widely known as other national sports teams. This year, they hope to make a wave.

items.title: The unorthodox coaching gambit that helped Matildas to greatest triumph
items.description: Former coach Tom Sermanni says "it wasn't his greatest look". But for its part in helping the Matildas to 2010 Asian Cup glory, it may well be the most consequential makeover in Australian football history.

items.title: When F1 cars crash, Albert Park's trauma team is called into action
items.description: Nestled away and out of view from the public sits the grand prix medical centre at Albert Park, with trauma specialists from Melbourne's Alfred Hospital on stand-by for the worst moments in motorsport.

items.title: How dingo behaviour on K'gari changed in years before Piper James's death
items.description: Piper James's tragic death is the third recorded fatality from a dingo attack in Australia. Here is a brief history of dingo management and interactions on K'gari.

items.title: Failed bid to extend wild dog fence angers rural graziers
items.description: Bourke Shire Mayor Lachlan Ford says finding out that a major extension of a wild dog barrier had been cancelled without consultation added insult to injury.

items.title: China accuses Australia of 'distorting facts' about helicopters' encounter
items.description: The Australian Defence Force says a Seahawk helicopter launched from HMAS Toowoomba was confronted by a Chinese helicopter and forced to "take evasion to maintain a safe flight".
